Magical Greenhouse

Magical Greenhouse is a cozy simulation game where you manage your own Potion Shop. Buy some magical plants, create potions and sell them to grow your business !

Thank you so much everyone for your support! This is the pre-release Version, if you liked it, you can discover the full game on Steam and support me by wishlisting it 💜

>>> Join us on Discord to discuss this game <<<

Gameplay:

Use the bottom Icons to navigate in the different parts of your business :
- In the Greenhouse, you can grow magical plants and harvest them
- The Workshop is the place were you can create some potions
- You can buy new Plants and Potion Recipes in the Shop
- Organize your own Store to sell your production
- Go to Sleep to allow your plants to grow



About the game :

A project handmade with love by Lya Mgtt (game design, dev & illustrations) and Yorack (dev) ♡
Subscribe to the mailing list to have the news before everyone : https://magical-greenhouse.com/   
Want to participate by giving us your feedback on the game ? Join the Discord ✨

Release note v0.6:

→ New Feature, Requests (you can now meet Villagers and help)
→ New Feature, Seasons (4 seasons and related requests)
→ New Feature, Pot Customization (you can now choose the color of your pots)
→ Feature Redesign, Onboarding (onboarding / tutorial guidance step by step)
→ Feature Update, the Store (you can now open the store when you want and it cost energy)
→ Content updates (new potions, new music, alembic animation, store animation...) → UX Improvements (plant modal, experimental crafting, settings, shop tabs, energy)
→ Bug Fixes (craft, displays...)

Complete release note available here :)

What's Next ? 

What you can expect for the next version:
→ New Feature, le Relationships (become friends with the Villagers!)
→ New Contents (requests, potions, villagers)
→ v1 Released on Steam in November
→ Join us on Discord!

Credits:

Illustrations by Lya Mgtt
Music by Samantha Van Der Sluis
A project supported by Game Crealab

Doom Ninja1 day ago

Cute game with potential. I see that you are on Steam now, and this is an old version, but here are my thoughts on this version anyway:

I think the resource management needs a lot of work. Energy reserves go up so quickly, and some days there isn't really even anything to do because of a lack of ingredients. I just end up dumping all my energy into plant XP. And usually just into a few plants, because ingredient values go up so hard that quickly the early game plants are basically irrelevant. I pick whatever expensive plant I have a potion recipe for.

It's kind of weird selling things is so all or nothing. If you simply never sell ingredients that you have a recipe for, it doesn't matter super much, but still. I want to hold things in reserve sometimes.

The shop seemed a little too simple, as well. You simply clear out your shelves, no matter what? I think you could greatly elaborate on that. Maybe a shop that is always open, and everything you have in there has its own chance of selling at the end of the day? And maybe having a greater variety of items means all sale chances go up (because more people visit)?

It would be more appealing if the game were structured such that all potions and ingredients stay relevant.

I wished potion brewing were more of a puzzle, with ingredients hinting at what they add to a potion, and potions hinting at details of how they work. To a degree, this is already in the game, but it's not consistent enough.

At some point I realized that potion prices are just twice ingredient prices, and potion recipe prices, as well as request payments, are twice the potion prices. This allowed me to work backwards from the price to figure out the ingredients of potions. This is not necessarily a bad thing!

Watering is kind of annoying. It's too complex an action to figure out which plants need it, and then to click their watering buttons. Unless I could have just let them dry out, then water. I never tried that.

It was a bummer for the demo to end like that. Let me go a bit longer and figure out the last potions, at least!

It's very cute that every potion and ingredient has its own sprites, the "normal" ones and the ones for being on the store shelves

This could just be a browser thing, but on a technical level I think switching scenes ought to be smoother. There isn't that much going on in each one.
